highlights.title: Middlesex beat Leicestershire to end 36-year List A trophy wait
highlights.summary: Middlesex ended a 36-year List A trophy drought by beating Leicestershire Foxes by 31 runs to win the Metro Bank One Day Cup in a low-scoring final at Trent Bridge.
body: Ryan Higgins made a superb maiden List A hundred from 115 balls with Harry Duke (55) backing him up as their 135-run sixth-wicket partnership steered Middlesex from 71-5 to 231 all out after Foxes all-rounder Ian Holland took 5-36 and wicketkeeper Ben Cox held five catches. Higgins and Duke were making their first appearances for Middlesex in this year's competition.

New Zealand international batter Nick Kelly hit an equally brilliant 103 (107 balls) to lead a Leicestershire fightback from 79-5 but it was not enough to haul his side over the line, Tom Helm (3-32) claiming his vital wicket in a superb late spell as the Foxes were bowled out for 200.

In an impressive performance in the field by Middlesex, Toby Roland-Jones (3-27) showed his quality and 21-year-old pace prospect Naayva Sharma (3-37) finished as the competition's leading wicket-taker with 20.
Against a background of turmoil off the field, the win is a first for Middlesex in a List A final since they beat Derbyshire to lift the 1990 Refuge Assurance Cup.

highlights.title: The Beekeeper Meets Ghost Recon in Jim Caviezel's New Action-Thriller Movie
highlights.summary: If anti-corporate ass-kicking cinema like Jason Statham 's The Beekeeper scratches your action movie itch, mark your calendars for Ghost Soldier, which blends Statham-style revenge action with Ghost Recon Future Soldier military tech.
body: Caviezel is best known for films like The Passion of the Christ and Sound of Freedom, but in Ghost Soldier, he's not turning the other cheek. Instead, he's wearing futuristic stealth cloaking technology and raining down hellfire on corporate hitmen. Caviezel does get some lines that nod to his religious roots. In the trailer for Ghost Soldier, he notes, coolly, "God will judge our enemies; I’ll just arrange the meeting."

When a powerful foreign corporation descends on his community determined to seize his and his neighbors’ land for a massive payday, Fitz takes action — he’s actually a former Special Forces soldier and advanced weapons developer. Armed with weapons no one has ever seen, a lifetime of lethal military training, and an unwavering code of justice, Fitz becomes the one thing his enemies never anticipated: a one-man war they can’t win.

Ghost Soldier is directed by William Eubank, who previously helmed Land of Bad and Underwater, from a screenplay by Chris Papasadero. Joining Jim Caviezel and Shea Whigham in the action-thriller are Olivia Thirlby ( Dredd ), Beau Knapp ( Tulsa King ), and Garret Dillahunt (who can also be seen currently riding a horse in HBO's Lanterns ).

highlights.summary: The president posted on Truth Social that he wanted to appoint an "AI czar" to lead a new "AI force." He made the announcement amid growing calls from across the political spectrum and even within the industry to pump the brakes on AI development.
body: He claimed without evidence that data centers are actually good for communities.

In the rambling post, Trump said that data centers were “wealthy and prestigious” and claimed without evidence that they raised salaries, lowered taxes, and made for safer streets in the communities in which they were built. He also related the AI Force to his creation of the Space Force, which he claimed was a “tremendous SUCCESS.”
The president gave no timeline or further details about the AI Force nor who might be tapped to lead it. Though he insisted that “Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!” for the position of AI Czar.

highlights.title: Smith thrashes Price to win World Series after Littler's shock exit
highlights.summary: Ross Smith thrashed Gerwyn Price 11-5 to become World Series of Darts Finals champion, while Luke Littler's hopes of a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 were dashed in the quarter-finals.
body: Smith won the last six legs, fired in 11 maximums, recorded back-to-back ton-plus finishes and went at 46 per cent on his doubles as he overwhelmed Price in Amsterdam on Sunday night to claim his second PDC major, after the 2022 European Championship.

Price, who missed a host of doubles in the back end of the match as his checkout percentage dropped to 26, has seven PDC majors in total, including three Grand Slams and the 2021 World Championship, but none since the World Series Finals in 2022.
Speaking bluntly afterwards on ITV4, the Welshman said: "I am playing some good darts, I am earning some good money. If I never win a major again I really don't care as long as I am doing well.

"I am gutted I've lost but if I never win another major then I have a good family, I have invested all my money. I really don't mind. I will be gutted for half an hour but on Tuesday I'll be in Tenerife.

highlights.title: 'Lanterns' Just Officially Settled a Major Question About the New DCU’s Canon
highlights.summary: One of the earliest scenes in Zack Snyder's Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice returns to the big climactic battle from Man of Steel. This time, we see it from Bruce Wayne ’s perspective on the street, where collapsing buildings and crashing Kryptonians look less like superhero spectacle and more…
body: In episode 6 of HBO’s Lanterns, the show wisely asks what regular people are doing to prepare for this kind of large-scale destruction in a DCU where it seems to happen regularly. A throwaway reference early in the episode quietly confirms one such event — and essentially canonizes another DC movie that was fairly murky before.

Ten years after handing Hal Jordan’s Green Lantern ring over to the Guardians, John Stewart has become an architect and founded Stewart Brothers in Midway City. The episode opens with him delivering a presentation to local government representatives that is essentially a series of football-stadium-sized panic rooms large enough to protect the city’s four million residents.

"We all saw what happened in Metropolis, right?” he asks. “But our city doesn't have a Superman." Then he wonders aloud what people might do the next time “a giant starfish” starts wreaking havoc. That’s not a throwaway hypothetical. Starro’s rampage, previously depicted in James Gunn’s The Suicide Squad, apparently also happened in the new DCU.

highlights.title: As Paramount Settlement Talks With States Progress, Some AGs Are Pushing for Stronger Restrictions
highlights.summary: On Sunday, settlement talks between Paramount and the state attorneys general that sued to block its Warner Bros. Discovery deal continued — but there was no resolution by the end of the day.
body: The terms discussed were said to include Paramount agreeing to operate Warner Bros.’ studio operations separately for a time (something Paramount chief David Ellison already said he was willing to do). Also on the table was a requirement that the merged Paramount-Warner Bros. release at least 30 films theatrically per year (a promise Ellison has already made, repeatedly), with financial penalties if they fail to hit that mark. In addition, the two sides also discussed a binding guarantee from Paramount that it would not relocate its existing California operations (as Ellison has threatened to do) and the formation of a third-party “editorial adviser” to oversee CNN and CBS News.

New York Attorney General Letitia James, for one, wants Paramount to commit to specific job-protection guarantees, including for employees at Warner Bros., sources confirmed. Paramount has claimed it would achieve $6 billion in cost savings by merging with WBD — and that would imply thousands of layoffs.

highlights.title: At The Nat Gala, Gabriela Hearst Celebrates Indigenous Matriarchs
highlights.summary: The Nat works to close the nature finance gap, and will next host a special gala in Paris in April 2027, Hearst announced on Sunday.
body: On Sunday night, celebrities, financiers, industry leaders and climate activists gathered in New York for the second annual Nat Gala. It was a starry affair supporting a decidedly un-starry subject: closing the approximately $700 billion nature finance gap.

Among the honorees was Dee Jay Two Bears, a filmmaker, artist and activist from the Standing Rock Sioux Tribe, who was heavily involved in the Dakota Access Pipeline protests from 2016 to 2017. While introducing Two Bears, and marking the 10th anniversary of Standing Rock, fashion designer Gabriela Hearst announced that the Nat Gala will head to Paris for the first time in April 2027, for an additional special event focused on the role of Indigenous matriarchs in galvanizing climate action and spearheading nature conservation.

While the main New York gala benefits the Blue Marine Foundation, Conservation International and Open Planet, the Paris event will specifically open up funding to Indigenous-led organizations, to be decided in due course.

highlights.title: No Dogs in Space is back to feed your need for obsessive music history
highlights.summary: In August, I wrote about my love of the music history podcast No Dogs in Space, but mourned the fact that there hadn't been a new episode in over two years. Little did I know that hosts Carolina Hidalgo and Marcus Parks were gearing up to announce the show's return with season four, Punk 2.0.
body: For the new season, Hidalgo and Parks decided it was time to get back to basics. Part of that was that they felt punk rock was where their passion and expertise were strongest. Parks said that they “wanted to go all over. I wanted to do Beethoven at one point,” but that “we realize like what we do best is tell a punk story, right? Not the punk story, but a punk story.“ But also, they said, that’s just where the most interesting stories are. After spending enormous amounts of time translating German into English for their experimental rock series, they realized that, often, the story behind the bands boils down to ”art school kids fucking around.”

There were a number of reasons why the new season took so long to come together. But one of the biggest is that the duo made a few false starts. Early on, the plan was to tackle the DC punk scene. Hidalgo told The Verge that “we worked on it for over six months” and that they planned to launch the series with Bad Brains. “And then we look into them,” Hidalgo said, “and they’re like, incredibly homophobic. Like, fire and brimstone … A lot of No Dogs bands like, they’re problematic, but that was like a really tough one to focus on.”

highlights.title: World model companies are keeping a lot of secrets
highlights.summary: Everyone in the world-models space is sitting on a pile of cash and a ton of buzz, but good luck getting anyone — from the founders to their own data suppliers — to tell you what they're actually building.
body: This week, I moderated a panel on world models at the All In conference (no relation to the podcast), and it gave me a chance to dig into one of the most mysterious corners of the AI world. The big players in the space are Yann LeCun’s AMI Labs and Fei-Fei Li’s World Labs — and while both have accumulated a lot of buzz and funding, they also rank pretty low on the trying-to-make-money scale.

At their core, world models are about automating spatial intelligence, so the field could head in lots of exciting and lucrative directions, from robotics to interactive video to more complex self-driving systems.

But when I started to press on where we would actually see the tech commercialized, things got foggy. The closest thing I found to an authority was Michael Rabbat, a co-founder of AMI Labs and the company’s VP of World Models, who joined me on the panel. But when I pressed him on exactly what the company was working on, he was cagey. “We’ll talk about it when we’re ready to talk about it.” Over email, he clarified, “We’re still in a research and building phase, so we’re not talking publicly about any product plans or timeline.”

body: Spaun became the first player since Byeong Hun An in 2015 to win the DP World Tour's flagship event on debut, posting a final-round 67 to claim a two-shot success over Rory McIlroy, Aaron Rai, Adam Scott and Manuel Elvira.

Last year's US Open champion also won on the PGA Tour earlier this season at the Valero Texas Open and finished 10th in the Presidents Cup qualification standings, having also made his Team USA debut in the Ryder Cup last September.

Spaun was controversially overlooked for a captain's pick by Brandt Snedeker in his line-up to face the International Team in the biennial contest, live from Thursday on Sky Sports, with the 36-year-old pleased to respond by claiming a statement victory.
"The stars aligned this week for me to come out on top," Spaun said. "I'm just grateful to have the opportunity and play well and give myself a chance and came out with a W.

body: Support for Warzone on PS4 and Xbox One will come to an end shortly after the launch of season 1 of Modern Warfare 4. The next mainline Call of Duty game launches on Oct. 23. Warzone will still be playable on PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X.

Activision and the Call of Duty teams ending support for Call of Duty: Warzone on PS4 and Xbox One won't come as much of a surprise to players on those platforms. After all, Modern Warfare 4 is also leaving last-gen consoles behind — this year's mainline Call of Duty game is bound for Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X.

Call of Duty: Warzone will continue to exist on current-gen platforms. Beginning with season 1 of Modern Warfare 4, Warzone will "integrate Modern Warfare 4 content and seasonal progression as part of a connected experience between both titles," a post attributed to Call of Duty Staff reads.

highlights.title: Christopher Kane and Mulberry make swaggering joint comeback at London fashion week
highlights.summary: Appointment of Kane as creative director signals the return of serious style ambition for former It-bag brand. With spicy leather mini-dresses and shoes with miniature axes for heels, two beloved British names made a swaggering joint comeback at London fashion week.
body: Fifteen years ago, Christopher Kane and Mulberry were two of the biggest shows on the line-up. Kane was the brilliant young designer who could find fashion in the most unlikely places: rubberised lace minis were inspired by “Princess Margaret on acid”; while illustrations from the 1972 classic The Joy of Sex appeared on slinky slip dresses. Mulberry was London’s home-grown It-bag brand: anyone who was anyone had a Bayswater or an Alexa.

On paper, it is an unlikely match. Mulberry is rooted in its Somerset factories and makes understated practical bags; Kane has a flair for bad-girl party dresses learned on the streets of Glasgow where he grew up.

Where they meet is leather. There were leather sheath dresses and elegantly spare leather car coats, as well as heeled loafers featuring Mulberry’s signature postman’s lock. Kane builds each collection around one visual motif – Frankenstein, gorillas, the reproductive organs of plants – and for this collection, took the castellated leather flaps of Mulberry’s Bayswater bags and turned them into notched hems and necklines. This was punchy, full-throttle fashion, accessorised with money-making bags and shoes.

highlights.title: No one is surprised that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang thinks AI fears are overblown.
highlights.summary: The man who may stand to make the most money from the AI boom seems to think he knows better than anyone else, including researchers who have studied and worked on AI for decades. In an interview with CBS Sunday Morning, he claimed there was a "0% chance" of AI being the end of the world.
body: He also claims that calls from CEOs like Anthropic’s Dario Amodei and OpenAI’s Sam Altman to slow down the development of AI are “not grounded in science.” He even argued that there was no need for new rules, laws, or guidelines, in the face of several high-profile cases in which models escaped containment and hacked other companies.

It’s not surprising that Huang was dismissive of the dangers posed by rogue AI and concerns about selling chips to China, or that he adamantly opposed new regulation. He is the CEO of the world’s most valuable company and number seven on Forbes ’ list of the richest people in the world. Just as importantly, his wealth has skyrocketed from an estimated $21 billion in 2023 to over $192 billion in 2026. Any hiccup in the unchecked expansion of the AI industry could slow his ascent.

highlights.title: ScrollEd wants to turn textbooks into TikTok
highlights.summary: ScrollEd turns textbooks into a scrollable, Instagram-like feed with video, audio, and quizzes. The Palo Alto startup, founded by student co-founders (and spouses) Utsav Gupta and Rebecca Neff, pitches at TechCrunch Disrupt.
body: Society has spent a lot of time bemoaning our digitally addled minds and goldfish-like attention spans, pointing the finger of blame at doomscrolling as the reason we can’t just sit down and read a book or study for exams. But what if the solution isn’t to stop scrolling, but to rethink what we’re scrolling through?

That’s the bet startup ScrollEd is making. The Palo Alto-based startup is pitching in the TechCrunch Disrupt Startup Battlefield 200 competition with the novel idea that if students won’t open a textbook, the textbook should open itself up to them — as a scroll.

ScrollEd has built an app that allows the user to turn any text file — including dry PDFs or text books — into a feed that feels a lot like Instagram Reels or TikTok. As you scroll, the content shows up as AI-generated video, audio, text, or even interactive quizzes. Swiping up surfaces a new topic, while swiping sideways lets you go deeper into the one you’re on, with a quiz waiting for you at the end.

body: “We were always prey. We were just kind of surviving at the appetite of our predators,” Joshua Corman, executive in residence for public safety and resilience at the Institute for Security and Technology (IST), told me last year. At the time, I was preoccupied with a Department of Homeland Security warning that Iranian actors and sympathizers could target the US with cyberattacks.

Last week, I called Corman up to chat about recent incidents of rogue AI agents orchestrating their own complex cyberattacks. Even AI executives are talking about whether the technology they’re building could grow so out of control that it triggers an apocalypse. If there is now a 10 percent chance of artificial intelligence one day killing all humans, as some AI developers warn, surely there’s a chance it could knock our lights out in the meantime?
“Any sociopath that wants to [attack] is now more powerful than they used to be.”

body: Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story is now streaming on Netflix. This review contains spoilers.

It’s just one of the many on-the-nose moments in Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story, the fourth installment in Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan’s true crime Netflix franchise.

This season explores the 1892 murders of wealthy Andrew Borden (Charlie Hunnam) and his wife Abby (Rebecca Hall) in Fall River, Massachusetts. Andrew’s youngest daughter Lizzie is tried for their murders but acquitted by an all-male jury thanks largely to shoddy police work and the belief that a woman was incapable of committing such a heinous, violent crime. highlights.title: Meta's Muse Is Better at Surveilling Than Helping Me
highlights.summary: The Muse app continues Meta’s trend of opting users into data collection for AI training. It also nudges you to share your bank account, email, and passport information.
body: I saw Meta’s latest app, Muse, cross-promoted on another Meta-owned platform, Instagram, and decided to download the AI assistant.

“Hand off everyday tasks like finding deals, booking reservations, and managing your inbox,” the pop-up read. “Muse keeps working while you get on with your day.” It’s free to use, and easily connects to other data sources, like my email and bank account. Muse’s default avatar is a beige-colored cross between an Ewok and a Labubu, with its arms outstretched, presumably to scoop up all my data.

Meta’s Muse is a mainstream version of AI agents already popular in Silicon Valley for automating personal tasks, like OpenClaw and Instinct. It’s a hit for the company: the Muse app has been downloaded over 900,000 times in its first week, according to Sensor Tower. The user experience is less like prompting a chatbot, and more like texting a friend with task requests—the AI agent acknowledges messages with a thumbs-up emoji and gets to work in the background. Muse is also available through Meta’s WhatsApp platform.
But after a few days with Muse, I’m convinced this AI tool is more obsessed with collecting data about me than actually getting stuff done.

highlights.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Will 'Easily Take Over 100 Hours' for Completionists to Beat, Director Teases
highlights.summary: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi teased that completionist playthroughs for the remake trilogy's conclusion could "easily take over a hundred hours" to beat.
body: The developer helping lead the charge on Cloud and the rest of the party's final assault against Sephiroth opened up about the size of the final chapter during an interview with GameSpot. We already suspected there would be a lot to do when Final Fantasy 7 Revelation launches for PC and consoles next year, but it sounds like those looking to see all Square Enix has to offer will be especially busy.

"In a standard playthrough from beginning to end, if I were to review and check every single asset and element in the game, it’ll easily take over a hundred hours," Hamaguchi said of his own playthroughs. "Obviously, I can't do that in each and every single playthrough. As the director, I don’t have enough time for that, so sometimes I would just skip combat and focus on checking the main story."

That's a lot of Final Fantasy 7 Revelation playtime. The two previous entries in the trilogy – Remake and Rebirth – proved to be large games in their own right, but the 2027 RPG finale will no doubt up the ante yet again. As Cloud, Tifa, Barret, Vincent Valentine, and the rest of the crew try to finish the fight against Sephiroth, players will use a giant airship known as the Highwind to travel.

Because Quan was just 12 years old when he booked the role of Short Round in the 1984 film (his first major
body: “One afternoon, I walked into the kitchen and found my parents standing together at the table,” Quan wrote in the memoir via Entertainment Weekly. “Mom was holding an envelope with my name printed across it. Dad had the papers that had been inside.”

“Back then, almost no actors got a piece of a movie’s profits,” Quan continued. “Even today, only the biggest stars do. That a kid like me, making his first film, would be included in something like that was unheard of. And ‘Temple of Doom’ wasn’t some small movie no one was expected to see. It was the sequel to a massive hit, a movie everyone knew would make a lot of money. That made their gesture even more generous.”

As a child, Quan also starred in Richard Donner’s 1985 film “The Goonies” as Data. He returned to the spotlight in 2023 after decades for “Everything Everywhere All at Once,” winning the Oscar for best supporting actor. His memoir, released Tuesday, details his early life fleeing Vietnam with his father, time in refugee camps, his life as a child actor and his triumphant return to the screen.

highlights.title: Victoria Starmer models clothes at London fashion week show
highlights.summary: Wife of former PM takes part in designer Edeline Lee’s show inspired by the Greek myth of Sisyphus. Victoria Starmer has taken part in a London fashion week show, in one of her first public appearances since her husband, Keir Starmer, stepped down as prime minister.
body: Lady Starmer appeared at Sunday’s Edeline Lee show. The London-based, Canadian British designer’s clothes are a favourite of the Princess of Wales, and have also been worn by celebrities including singer Taylor Swift and actor and screenwriter Phoebe Waller-Bridge.

Lee’s spring/summer 2027 show took place in the unusual setting of a north London school sports hall. Starmer wore a bright turquoise knitted midi dress with a high neckline, pleated detailing and short, sculptural sleeves, paired with white block-heeled shoes, with her hair worn in loose waves.

Rather than preparations for the show taking place backstage in the usual way, in Lee’s unique show, models were fitted and adjusted in full view of the audience, dancers rehearsed beside the catwalk, while a drone followed proceedings from the high ceiling of the gymnasium.

Starmer was photographed having her makeup done beside the catwalk, against a backdrop of a football net, with makeup and hair products spread out over a table in front of her. Ballerinas stretched beside the catwalk and synchronised swimming-inspired dancers performed in bright red costumes as part of the show, in the school in Chalk Farm.
